summary.intent: Write an automated Playwright e2e spec for the share itemName lazy-backfill UAT (Phase 48 REQ-4), covering two-party setup, legacy-row seeding, owner-upload backfill trigger, at-rest ciphertext assertion, and recipient display — then run it against the local full stack and commit it.
summary.outcome: The spec was written (tests/web-e2e/tests/share-itemname-backfill.spec.ts), all 7 steps passed in 52.1s against the local stack proving the null→ciphertext state transition, lint/typecheck passed, but the commit was still pending at transcript end due to a wedged 1Password SSH signer requiring a restart.

repo: backfillSentShareItemNames fires ONLY via the SDK getCoveringShares callback (useAuth.ts:324-331) → findCoveringShares → fetchAllSentShares; the sole UI-reachable trigger is any owner file upload. ShareDialog bypasses fetchAllSentShares entirely by calling sharesControllerGetSentShares directly.

CreateShareDto.itemNameEncrypted is @IsOptional (create-share.dto.ts:91) so legacy NULL rows are creatable via direct API POST, but the web createShare() always sends ciphertext (share.service.ts:251-258) — legacy rows cannot be produced through the UI.

The recipient-decrypt path falls back to plaintext on failure (share.service.ts:121), so a broken ciphertext still renders the correct display name. Recipient assertion alone is insufficient; it must be paired with the GET /shares/sent null→hex assertion.

backfillSentShareItemNames runs fire-and-forget (share.service.ts:394) and the SDK caches fetchAllSentShares for 30s; specs must poll GET /shares/sent for the column to flip rather than asserting synchronously.
GET /shares/sent returns itemNameEncrypted as hex or null (shares.controller.ts:147), making it a strong in-harness proxy for at-rest ciphertext without needing a pg connection.

web-e2e has no pg/DataSource (absent from tests/web-e2e/package.json), so literal raw-bytea Postgres reads require either adding a pg util or a test-only debug endpoint; the Compose stack exposes 5432 postgres/postgres.
The repo enforces signed commits via 1Password op-ssh-sign; in sandboxed Bash environments the signer cannot be reached and commits fail silently or hang, requiring unsandboxed retries.
After gh pr create a bot pushes a chore(release): set release targets commit to the branch; the flow requires fetch + rebase + push before merging to avoid divergence.
The API runs in watch mode locally and auto-reloads changes; probe a new endpoint with a 401 vs 404 response to confirm it has loaded before running e2e tests.

code.finding: getCoveringShares is called unconditionally before the length check on every reWrapNewItems (uploadFile) invocation — every owner upload triggers the backfill over all sent shares.
@IsOptional on itemNameEncrypted — omitting this field in a POST /shares body produces a legacy NULL row, which is the only way to seed legacy state since the web layer always populates it.
shouldBackfill returns false when ciphertext is already present — backfill is idempotent; re-triggering leaves the column unchanged.
Recipient display falls back to plaintext itemName when itemNameEncrypted is null (legacy path) and decrypts the ciphertext when present — false-pass risk if ciphertext is malformed.
backfillSentShareItemNames call is void/fire-and-forget; callers do not await it, requiring polling in tests.
page.evaluate(fetch) + POST /auth/refresh pattern for obtaining access tokens inside browser context — reused as the base for the seedLegacyShare helper.
createWalletTestAccount(browser, name) is the established two-identity pattern; use with test.describe.serial for Alice/Bob specs.
Method is getSharedItemNames() (not getAllSharedItemNames() as the synthesis initially stated); getSharedItem(name) exists at line 64.

workflow: A fan-out workflow (4 parallel investigators → synthesis → adversarial verifier) is the right tool for empirically determining test harness feasibility before writing a spec — it caught false method names and the false-pass risk the synthesis missed.
Prove state transitions, not just final state: asserting null before seeding and ciphertext ≠ plaintext after backfill eliminates the false-pass risk from the plaintext fallback path.
For fire-and-forget async backend operations in Playwright, poll an API endpoint with a timeout rather than using waitForResponse or fixed sleeps.
When a signed commit hangs with op-ssh-sign, check for rc=124 (timeout/hang) vs rc=128 (buffer error) — the latter requires restarting the 1Password app, not just retrying.

friction: 1Password op-ssh-sign SSH signer wedged twice: first timed out (rc=124), then failed with 'failed to fill whole buffer' (rc=128), requiring a full 1Password app restart before the commit could land.
Sandboxed Bash cannot reach the 1Password SSH agent, so signed commits must be retried in an unsandboxed context — not obvious from the failure mode.

The workflow result was truncated in the task notification (26k chars cut), requiring a separate file read to get the adversarial verifier's corrections including the wrong method name (getAllSharedItemNames vs getSharedItemNames).
The initial 'human-only' label for the UAT was wrong and required a full harness audit to disprove — the cost of labeling something out-of-scope without checking.
